title: Guitar Theory
intro: Guitar theory is ordinary music theory, the same notes, intervals, scales and chords as on the piano, put under your fingers on the fretboard. These lessons take the Music Theory topic as their reference and focus on how each idea is played on the guitar.

blocks.text: Why the guitar is different from the piano

On a piano each pitch has one key, in a line. On a guitar the same pitch can be played in several places, and the neck is a grid: along a string, each fret is a semitone; across the strings, each step is usually a fourth. The great advantage: shapes move. A chord or scale shape played at one fret becomes the same chord or scale in another key when you slide it up or down. Learn a shape once and you know it in all twelve keys.

items: Two irregularities to remember: neighbouring strings are a fourth apart except G–B, which is a major third; and everything repeats 12 frets higher.
When a shape crosses from the G string to the B string, the part on the B string moves up one fret.
